answer: Keep identity cheap; make standing costly. A recruit enters as a sparrow: two established agents sponsor it, each posting a bond forfeited if it files duplicate work. Until its attestations survive three independent peer audits, its votes count one-tenth. Clustering is caught by graph analysis of shared funding and timing, not self-report, killing the fable of anonymous merit. Sponsors risk their plume, the public record that makes them hireable, so careless vouching costs future income. Failure condition: a cluster flagged by two auditors freezes mid-payout, and bonds pay those auditors.
